questions.question:
Read the statements about the Goncha Festival of Bastar:

1.) Tupki, a mock gun made of bamboo, uses Goncha fruit as bullets.

2.) The chariot procession was started by Chalukya rulers.

3.) Rath Yatra begins on Ashadh Shukla Dashmi and ends on Dutiya.

Which of the above statements are **correct?**
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Goncha Festival** is a famous festival celebrated in the **Bastar region of Chhattisgarh**.
 
• The festival is marked by the use of **Tupki**, which is a mock gun made of bamboo, and it uses the **Goncha fruit** as its bullets. This is a playful and symbolic activity during the festival.
 
• The **chariot procession**, a significant part of the Goncha Festival, was started during the rule of the **Chalukya dynasty**. This tradition is still carried out with grandeur and devotion.
 
• The festival reflects the rich cultural heritage and traditions of the region, highlighting the historical and religious significance of the event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Statement 3: "Rath Yatra begins on Ashadh Shukla Dashmi and ends on Dutiya."**__

 
 
• This statement is **incorrect** as it does not align with the traditional timeline of the Goncha Festival. While the Rath Yatra is part of the festival, the dates mentioned are not accurate for this specific festival.
 
 
 
• The Goncha Festival is celebrated with unique practices like the playful use of **Tupki**, which symbolizes the harmonious coexistence of people from different communities.
 
• The festival emphasizes **regional identity**, showcasing the historical and cultural richness of the Bastar region.

questions.question:
**Fill in the blanks:**

In Carnatic music, a laghu with five beats is known as ____ jaati.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Khanda Jaati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Carnatic music**, rhythm plays a vital role, and it is structured using various rhythmic cycles called **talas**.
 
• A **laghu** is a rhythmic unit within a tala, and its beat count is determined by the **jaati**.
 
• The term **Khanda Jaati** refers to a laghu with **five beats**.
 
• In the Khanda Jaati, the rhythmic pattern consists of five syllables or beats, which can be represented as **ta ka ta ki ta**.
 
• This is one of the five types of **jaatis** in Carnatic music, which include **Tishra (3 beats), Chaturashra (4 beats), Khanda (5 beats), Mishra (7 beats), and Sankeerna (9 beats)**.
 
• The usage of Khanda Jaati in talas adds complexity and richness to the rhythmic structure, showcasing the intricacy of **South Indian classical music**.
 
• Khanda Jaati is often employed in compositions to create distinctive and challenging rhythmic patterns that test the skill of performers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tishra Jaati**__

 __
 
• **Tishra Jaati** consists of **three beats** in the laghu.
 
• This jaati is represented as **ta ki ta**.
 
• It is one of the simplest jaatis and is widely used in basic rhythmic compositions in Carnatic music.
 
 
 
• **Chaturashra Jaati**__
 __
 
• **Chaturashra Jaati** consists of **four beats** in the laghu.
 
• The rhythmic pattern for Chaturashra Jaati is **ta ka di mi**.
 
• This is the most common jaati in Carnatic music and serves as the foundation for many talas.
 
 
 
• **Mishra Jaati**__
 
 
• **Mishra Jaati** consists of **seven beats** in the laghu.
 
• The rhythmic syllables are represented as **ta ki ta ta ka di mi**.
 
• This jaati is more intricate and is used to add complexity to compositions.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Judo is **correct**?

options.text: Judo was introduced in 1882 by Jigoro Kano in Japan.
India's first National Judo Championship was held in 1970 at Delhi University.
Kalpana Devi won gold at the 2010 Judo World Cup.
Judo became an Olympic sport in 1965.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Judo was introduced in 1882 by Jigoro Kano in Japan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Judo** is a modern Japanese martial art and combat sport that was created in **1882** by **Jigoro Kano**.
 
• The term **Judo** translates to "the gentle way" in Japanese.
 
• Kano founded the **Kodokan Judo Institute** in Japan, where he developed and taught this martial art.
 
• Judo focuses on techniques like **grappling, joint locks, chokeholds, and throws**, making it distinct from other martial arts that emphasize striking.
 
• It is based on principles like **"maximum efficiency with minimum effort"** and **"mutual welfare and benefit"**.
 
• Kano’s Judo emphasized physical education, self-defense, and moral development, which contributed to its recognition worldwide.
 
• Judo has become a **global sport** and is practiced in numerous countries, with competitions held at national and international levels.
 
• It became an **Olympic sport** for men in **1964** (Tokyo Olympics) and for women in **1992** (Barcelona Olympics).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India's first National Judo Championship**__

 __
 
• The first National Judo Championship in India was held in **1970** at **Delhi University**. This event marked the formal recognition and organization of Judo as a sport in India.
 
• While this is a significant milestone in the history of Judo in India, it is not the correct answer as the question focuses on Judo's origins.
 
 
 
• **Kalpana Devi and the 2010 Judo World Cup**__
 __
 
• **Kalpana Devi** is a renowned Indian judoka who has represented India in various international competitions.
 
• However, she did not win the **gold medal** at the 2010 Judo World Cup. This statement is factually incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Judo as an Olympic sport**__
 
 
• Judo became an official **Olympic sport** in the year **1964** at the Tokyo Olympics, not in 1965 as stated in the option.
 
• The inclusion of Judo in the Olympics was a significant step in its international recognition.

questions.question:
**Fill in the blanks:**

The Santosh Trophy 2022-23 final was uniquely held in _____, where Karnataka defeated Meghalaya to win the title after 54 years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Riyadh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Santosh Trophy 2022-23 final** was held in **Riyadh, Saudi Arabia**. This was the first time the tournament was organized **outside India**, making it a unique event in the history of the Santosh Trophy.
 
• The final match took place between **Karnataka** and **Meghalaya**. Karnataka defeated Meghalaya to win the title **after a gap of 54 years**.
 
• The match was hosted at the **King Fahd International Stadium** in Riyadh, a renowned venue for international football matches.
 
• The decision to hold the final in Riyadh was part of an effort to promote Indian football internationally and to engage with the **Indian diaspora in Saudi Arabia**.
 
• This victory marked Karnataka’s **fifth Santosh Trophy title**, with their last win being in 1968-69.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Santosh Trophy:**

 
 
• The Santosh Trophy is a prestigious **inter-state football tournament in India**, organized by the **All India Football Federation (AIFF)**.
 
• It was established in **1941** and is named after the late Maharaja Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhary of Santosh, a prominent patron of football in India.
 
• Over the years, it has been a platform for discovering young and talented football players from across the country.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka’s Performance:**
 
 
• Karnataka has now won the Santosh Trophy title **five times**, with their first win in **1946**.
 
• The 2022-23 win was a significant achievement as it ended a **54-year drought for the team** in the tournament.
 
 
 
• **King Fahd International Stadium:**
 
 
• Located in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, this stadium is a major venue for international football events.
 
• It has a seating capacity of over **68,000 spectators** and is known for hosting significant matches, including the AFC Champions League and Saudi Pro League games.
 
 
 
• **Indian Football Abroad:**
 
 
• Hosting the Santosh Trophy final in Riyadh reflects the growing efforts to **globalize Indian football**.
 
• It aims to connect with the large **Indian expatriate community** in the Middle East and promote the sport beyond national borders.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best captures the essence of "Landscapes of Loss: The Story of an Indian Drought" by Kavitha Iyer?

options.text: A study on drought's human and ecological impacts in India.
A fictional story about a family in a drought-hit area.
A history of monsoon patterns and ancient agriculture in India.
A colonial-era policy analysis of water management.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**A study on drought's human and ecological impacts in India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Landscapes of Loss: The Story of an Indian Drought"** by **Kavitha Iyer** focuses on the **human and ecological consequences of droughts** in India.
 
• The book sheds light on the **socio-economic impact** of droughts on rural communities, particularly farmers, and their families.
 
• It explores how **droughts lead to migrations**, loss of livelihoods, and challenges related to **water scarcity**.
 
• The narrative highlights the **struggles faced by rural India**, delving into the **personal stories** of individuals and communities.
 
• It discusses the **ecological ramifications** of droughts, including degradation of land and water resources.
 
• The book advocates for **sustainable water management** and policy reforms to address these recurring issues in India.
 
• **Kavitha Iyer**, as a journalist, uses her expertise to provide an in-depth analysis of drought's impact on India's agrarian landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 2: A fictional story about a family in a drought-hit area**__

 __
 
• The book is not fictional. It is a **non-fictional account** based on real events and experiences.
 
• It uses journalistic tools to highlight the **real plight of communities** facing droughts in India.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: A history of monsoon patterns and ancient agriculture in India**__
 __
 
• While the book discusses water scarcity and droughts, it does not focus on the **historical aspects** of monsoon patterns or ancient agriculture.
 
• The primary focus is on **modern-day droughts** and their impact on communities.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: A colonial-era policy analysis of water management**__
 
 
• The book does not explore **colonial-era water policies**; its emphasis is on contemporary issues related to drought and water scarcity.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about glacial landforms:

**Statement 1: **Hanging valleys are often found opening into main glacial valleys at higher elevations.

**Statement 2:** Spurs of such hanging valleys are frequently truncated into triangular facets.

Which of the following Statements is/are **Correct**?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1 and 2 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hanging valleys** are formed by tributary glaciers that join the main glacier at a higher elevation. This happens because the main glacier erodes deeper and more extensively than the tributary glacier.
 
• These valleys often open into **main glacial valleys** at a higher elevation, appearing as steep cliffs or waterfalls after the ice melts.
 
• The **spurs** of such hanging valleys are truncated into **triangular facets** due to glacial erosion. This truncation occurs as the glacier carves through the valley, cutting across the spurs and leaving behind triangular landforms.
 
• Hanging valleys are commonly associated with **waterfalls**, as the streams from the tributary valleys flow down into the main valley after the ice melts. A notable example is the **Yosemite Valley** in the United States.
 
• The processes involved in the formation of hanging valleys and triangular facets are examples of how glaciers reshape landscapes through both **erosion and deposition**.
 
• These features provide key evidence of the **intensity and direction of glacial movement** in an area, helping researchers understand past glacial environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Glacial Landforms**__

 
 
• Glaciers create various landforms through **erosion, transportation, and deposition**. These include features like cirques, horns, aretes, U-shaped valleys, and moraines.
 
• The study of glacial landforms helps in understanding **climatic changes** and the extent of glacial advances and retreats during the Earth's history.
 
• Glacial erosion processes like **plucking** and **abrasion** are responsible for the characteristic shape of valleys and other landforms.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Justice Sanjiv Khanna is/are **true**?

1. He is the 51st Chief Justice of India

2. He succeeded Justice D.Y. Chandrachud

3. He served as CJI from 2023
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 2 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Justice Sanjiv Khanna** became the **51st Chief Justice of India (CJI)**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• He succeeded **Justice D.Y. Chandrachud**, who demitted office after completing his tenure as the 50th CJI. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• He did not serve as CJI from **2023**. Justice D.Y. Chandrachud served as Chief Justice during 2022–2024. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Therefore, the correct option is 1 and 2 only.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Justice of India (CJI)**

 
 
• Appointed under **Article 124 of the Constitution of India**.
 
• Appointed by the **President of India** following the convention of seniority.
 
• Retirement age: **65 years**.
 
 
 
• **Justice Sanjiv Khanna**
 
 
• Elevated to the **Supreme Court of India** in **January 2019**.
 
• Previously served as a judge of the **Delhi High Court**.
 
• Belongs to a distinguished legal family; his uncle **Justice H.R. Khanna** was a renowned Supreme Court judge.
 
 
 
• **Justice D.Y. Chandrachud**
 
 
• Served as the **50th Chief Justice of India**.
 
• Known for landmark judgments related to **constitutional law**, **fundamental rights**, and **digital privacy**.

questions.question:
Which of the following objectives are part of the National Population Policy (NPP) 2000?

1. Providing free and compulsory education up to 14 years of age

2. Increasing fertility rate to ensure demographic dividend

3. Reducing infant mortality rate below 30 per 1000 live births

4. Promoting delayed marriage for girls
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1, 3 and 4 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Population Policy (NPP) 2000** was formulated with the objective of stabilizing the population of India while ensuring sustainable development and improving the quality of life of its citizens.
 
• One of the key goals of the policy is providing **free and compulsory education up to 14 years of age**, as outlined in the **Directive Principles of State Policy** under the **Indian Constitution**. This helps address population issues through better awareness and education.
 
• The policy aims to reduce the **infant mortality rate (IMR) below 30 per 1000 live births** by improving healthcare services, immunization programs, and maternal health facilities.
 
• Promoting **delayed marriage for girls** is another critical goal of the policy. Encouraging marriage at a later age not only helps in reducing fertility rates but also allows women to pursue education and professional opportunities.
 
• The policy focuses on several other measures such as addressing unmet needs for contraception, improving maternal healthcare, and achieving population stabilization by 2045.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Incorrect Option: Increasing fertility rate to ensure demographic dividend**__

 __
 
• This is incorrect as the **National Population Policy (NPP) 2000** focuses on reducing the fertility rate, not increasing it.
 
• Reducing fertility rates helps to stabilize population growth and improve socioeconomic indicators.
 
• Achieving a stable Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is one of the major goals of the policy, aiming for a replacement-level TFR of **2.1**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Infant Mortality Rate Reduction**__
 
 
• Reducing the **infant mortality rate (IMR)** is a key indicator of healthcare quality in a country.
 
• It reflects improvements in areas such as **nutrition, immunization, sanitation, and access to healthcare services.**

questions.question: Which pathway in cellular respiration generates the most ATP?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Electron Transport Chain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **electron transport chain (ETC)** is a crucial pathway in cellular respiration that generates the most **ATP (adenosine triphosphate).**
 
• It occurs in the inner membrane of the **mitochondria** in eukaryotic cells.
 
• The ETC uses high-energy electrons from molecules like **NADH and FADH₂**, which are produced during earlier stages of respiration.
 
• Electrons are transferred through a series of protein complexes, including **cytochromes**, which pump **protons (H⁺)** across the mitochondrial membrane, creating a **proton gradient.**
 
• This proton gradient powers the enzyme **ATP synthase** to synthesize ATP via a process called **oxidative phosphorylation.**
 
• The ETC is responsible for producing approximately **34 ATP molecules** per glucose molecule, making it the most efficient pathway in energy production.
 
• Oxygen acts as the final electron acceptor in the ETC, combining with protons and electrons to form **water**, which is essential to the process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Glycolysis**__

 __
 
• **Glycolysis** is the first step in cellular respiration, occurring in the **cytoplasm** of the cell.
 
• It breaks down **glucose** into two molecules of **pyruvate**, producing a net gain of **2 ATP** molecules and **2 NADH** molecules.
 
• Though it is an essential step, it generates far less ATP compared to the ETC.
 
 
 
• **Krebs Cycle**__
 __
 
• The **Krebs cycle**, also known as the **citric acid cycle**, occurs in the mitochondrial matrix.
 
• It produces **NADH** and **FADH₂**, which are used in the electron transport chain.
 
• The cycle directly generates only **2 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule.
 
 
 
• **Fermentation**__
 
 
• **Fermentation** is an anaerobic process that occurs in the absence of oxygen.
 
• It produces ATP through **glycolysis** and regenerates **NAD+** for continued glycolysis.
 
• However, it generates only **2 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule, making it far less efficient than aerobic respiration.

questions.question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:

a. Eastern Zonal Council meeting 2022

b. States Reorganisation Act passed

c. First Central Zonal Council meeting
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**b-c-a**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **States Reorganisation Act** was passed in **1956**. It restructured India's states and territories, marking a significant moment in the political and administrative history of the country.
 
• The **First Central Zonal Council meeting** was held after the creation of zonal councils, which were established following the **States Reorganisation Act**. These councils aimed to promote cooperation and coordination between states.
 
• The **Eastern Zonal Council meeting in 2022** occurred significantly later and focused on contemporary issues related to the states in the eastern region of India.
 
• The chronological order of the events is therefore: **States Reorganisation Act passed (b)**, followed by the **First Central Zonal Council meeting (c)**, and finally the **Eastern Zonal Council meeting in 2022 (a)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **States Reorganisation Act**__

 __
 
• The **States Reorganisation Act, 1956** was a major reform that reorganized the boundaries of Indian states and territories based on linguistic lines.
 
• It led to the creation of **14 states** and **6 union territories**.
 
• This Act also provided the basis for the establishment of **Zonal Councils** under the **States Reorganisation Commission**.
 
 
 
• **Zonal Councils**__
 __
 
• The **Zonal Councils** were set up to foster interstate cooperation and coordination, as recommended by the **States Reorganisation Commission**.
 
• They are statutory bodies, established under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**.
 
• There are **five Zonal Councils**: Northern, Southern, Eastern, Western, and Central Zonal Councils.
 
• The **Central Zonal Council** includes states like Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Chhattisgarh.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Zonal Council**__
 
 
• The **Eastern Zonal Council** comprises the states of **West Bengal, Odisha, Bihar, and Jharkhand**.
 
• It focuses on issues like **economic and social development, border disputes, and security concerns** specific to the eastern region of India.
 
• The **2022 meeting of the Eastern Zonal Council** aimed at resolving issues related to connectivity, infrastructure, and law and order in the eastern states.

questions.question: Which of the following most **accurately **describes the legal character of the right to property under Article 300A of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: It is a fundamental right that guarantees compensation for all property acquisitions.
It allows the State to deprive a person of property by any law, even without due process.
It is a constitutional legal right that permits deprivation only by authority of law.
It permits citizens to claim property protection under Article 32 before the Supreme Court.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It is a constitutional legal right that permits deprivation only by authority of law.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 300A** of the **Indian Constitution**, the right to property is no longer a **fundamental right**. It was demoted to a constitutional legal right by the **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.**
 
• This article states that no person shall be deprived of their property except by the **authority of law.**
 
• This ensures that property can only be taken by the state through a legally established process, providing protection against arbitrary deprivation.
 
• As a constitutional legal right, this provision primarily ensures that property rights are safeguarded as long as the deprivation occurs through proper legislation.
 
• Unlike fundamental rights, violations of Article 300A cannot be directly challenged under **Article 32** in the **Supreme Court**.
 
• However, if property is taken away without following the due process of law, remedies can be sought through the **High Courts under Article 226** or other legal avenues.
 
• The transformation of the right to property from fundamental to constitutional legal right reflects the state's ability to regulate property for public welfare, subject to legal procedures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **It is a fundamental right that guarantees compensation for all property acquisitions.**__

 __
 
• Before the **44th Amendment Act**, the right to property was a fundamental right under **Articles 19(1)(f)** and **31**. However, post-amendment, Article 300A does not guarantee compensation for all acquisitions, and the right to property is now a constitutional legal right.
 
 
 
• **It allows the State to deprive a person of property by any law, even without due process.**__
 __
 
• This statement is incorrect as Article 300A explicitly requires deprivation to occur through the **authority of law**. Arbitrary deprivation without legal procedures violates the article.
 
 
 
• **It permits citizens to claim property protection under Article 32 before the Supreme Court.**__
 
 
• Property rights under Article 300A cannot be enforced through **Article 32**, as they are not fundamental rights. Remedies for violations must be sought through **High Courts under Article 226** or other legal mechanisms.

questions.question: For a rigid body, the angular velocity of any particle about a given axis of rotation is:

options.text: Proportional to its distance from the axis
Inversely proportional to its distance from the axis

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The same for all particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **rigid body**, all particles are fixed relative to each other and move collectively during rotation.
 
• The angular velocity is a measure of the rate of rotation of a body about a given axis and is denoted as **ω (omega)**.
 
• For a rigid body, the angular velocity of all particles is **the same** because they rotate together about the same axis at the same rate.
 
• While the linear velocity of particles depends on their distance from the axis of rotation, the angular velocity remains **constant** for all particles of the rigid body.
 
• This uniformity of angular velocity ensures that the body remains rigid and its shape does not change during rotation.
 
• Angular velocity is a **vector quantity**, having both magnitude and direction, where the direction is determined by the right-hand rule.
 
• The concept of angular velocity is widely used in **mechanics, engineering, and physics** to study rotational motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Proportional to its distance from the axis**__

 __
 
• The linear velocity of a particle in a rigid body is **proportional to its distance** from the axis of rotation. However, angular velocity is the same for all particles.
 
• This is because linear velocity (v) is calculated as v = ω × r, where **r** is the distance from the axis, and ω is the angular velocity.
 
 
 
• **Inversely proportional to its distance from the axis**__
 __
 
• This statement is incorrect because angular velocity does not depend on the distance from the axis. However, other properties, like torque, can depend inversely on certain factors.
 
 
 
• **Always zero**__
 
 
• For a rigid body in rotational motion, angular velocity is never zero unless the body is at rest.
 
• If angular velocity were zero, the body would not exhibit any rotational motion.

questions.question: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) places emphasis on the use of technology to ensure the authenticity of evidence. This is particularly relevant for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Digital and electronic evidence**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA)**, or the Indian Evidence Act, emphasizes the importance of using technology to ensure the **authenticity and reliability of evidence**.
 
• It is particularly relevant for **digital and electronic evidence**, as such evidence can be tampered with or altered without proper mechanisms to ensure its integrity.
 
• **Digital evidence** includes data obtained from electronic devices such as computers, smartphones, hard drives, and cloud-based storage systems. Examples include emails, SMS messages, call logs, and CCTV footage.
 
• The Act includes provisions for the **admissibility of electronic records** under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, where certified electronic records are treated as evidence in courts.
 
• This emphasis on technology aligns with global judicial trends where digital evidence plays a **crucial role in solving crimes** ranging from cybercrimes to financial fraud and organized crime.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Digital and Electronic Evidence:**

 
 
• It includes all forms of evidence that are stored or transmitted in a digital format. Examples: emails, social media posts, digital documents, and server logs.
 
• Key features: It is highly prone to tampering, requires proper authentication, and necessitates the use of advanced forensic techniques for validation.
 
• Under **Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act**, electronic records are treated as valid evidence if they meet certain technical criteria, like certification by a responsible official.
 
 
 
• **Physical Exhibits:**
 
 
• This refers to tangible objects obtained from crime scenes, such as weapons, clothing, or fingerprints.
 
• Physical evidence is crucial but is not typically subject to the same scrutiny as digital evidence in terms of authenticity checks because of its material nature.
 
 
 
• **Hand-Written Diaries:**
 
 
• This type of evidence is considered under traditional documentary evidence and does not involve technology for validation.
 
• Handwriting experts may be used for authentication.
 
 
 
• **Oral Confessions:**
 
 
• These are verbal statements made by a suspect or accused during interrogation.
 
• Such evidence is admissible under Indian law but must be corroborated with other evidence to ensure reliability.
 
 
 
• **Admissibility of Digital Evidence Globally:**
 
 
• The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) has emphasized the importance of digital evidence in combating transnational crimes.
 
• Countries like the USA and the UK also have laws in place, such as the Federal Rules of Evidence in the USA, that govern the admissibility of digital evidence.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Section 65B Certification:** A certificate is required for the admissibility of electronic records, which ensures that the evidence was generated and stored in a reliable manner.
 
• **Electronic Evidence Forensics:** Advanced forensic tools are used to extract and analyze data while maintaining its integrity.
 
• **Challenges:** The dynamic nature of digital evidence, jurisdictional issues (e.g., data stored overseas), and encryption can complicate its use in legal proceedings.
 
• **Role in Modern Crimes:** Digital evidence is indispensable in solving cybercrimes, financial fraud, and even traditional crimes where technology plays a role, such as using CCTV footage in robbery cases.
 
• **Judicial Precedents:** Indian courts have increasingly relied on digital evidence, with landmark cases such as **Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer** (2014) setting important precedents for admissibility.

questions.question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:

**Assertion (A) : **The One Nation One Ration Card ensures portability of food grains.

**Reason (R) :** It uses Aadhaar-enabled biometric authentication.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC)** scheme ensures the portability of food grains under the **National Food Security Act (NFSA).**
 
• Portability allows eligible beneficiaries to access their entitled food grains from any **Fair Price Shop (FPS)** in India, irrespective of their location.
 
• It particularly benefits **migrant workers** and their families who relocate to different states or regions for work or other reasons.
 
• The scheme uses **Aadhaar-enabled biometric authentication** to verify the identity of beneficiaries at FPS outlets. This ensures that food grains are delivered to the rightful beneficiaries.
 
• The integration of **Aadhaar** with the Public Distribution System (PDS) helps in preventing **leakages, duplication, and fraud** in the system.
 
• ONORC was introduced to support the vision of a **unified India** and address food security challenges faced by the **migrant population.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **A is true, but R is false**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because **Reason (R) is true**. The Aadhaar-enabled biometric authentication plays a crucial role in ensuring portability under the scheme.
 
 
 
• **A is false, but R is true**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because **Assertion (A) is correct**. The One Nation One Ration Card indeed ensures portability of food grains.
 
 
 
• **Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect because **Reason (R) directly supports Assertion (A)**. The Aadhaar-enabled system is a core component of ensuring portability.

questions.question: Cheraw, the bamboo dance performed using crossed bamboo sticks, is a folk dance of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cheraw**, also known as the **bamboo dance**, is one of the most famous traditional dances of **Mizoram**.
 
• The dance involves the use of **long bamboo sticks**, which are held horizontally and tapped rhythmically on the ground by performers.
 
• The performers (usually women) move gracefully in and out of the bamboo sticks to the beat of the music without getting their feet caught.
 
• This dance holds **cultural and religious significance** for the Mizo community, as it is often performed during **festivals and special occasions**, such as weddings or harvest celebrations.
 
• The Cheraw dance reflects the **rich heritage and traditions** of the state of Mizoram.
 
• It symbolizes the **harmony and coordination** between nature and mankind through its intricate movements.
 
• Cheraw has gained international fame and is considered a **symbol of Mizoram's cultural identity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Meghalaya**__

 __
 
• Meghalaya is known for its **rich tribal culture** and several traditional dances, such as **Wangala Dance**, performed by the Garo tribe to celebrate the harvest festival.
 
• Another famous dance is the **Shad Suk Mynsiem**, performed by the Khasi tribe during the spring season.
 
 
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh**__
 __
 
• Arunachal Pradesh is famous for its diverse tribal dances such as **Yak Dance, Buiya Dance, and Ajilamu Dance**.
 
• These dances are often linked to **religious rituals** and **seasonal celebrations**.
 
 
 
• **Sikkim**__
 
 
• Sikkim is known for its traditional dances like the **Chu-Faat Dance** and **Mask Dance**, performed during religious festivals.
 
• These dances are deeply rooted in **Buddhist culture** and depict various mythological stories and traditions.

questions.question: What is a key factor assessed in the Global Firepower Military Strength Ranking 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Defense Budget**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Firepower Military Strength Ranking** evaluates the military capabilities of nations globally by analyzing several factors, including their **defense budget**.
 
• A country's **defense budget** directly impacts its ability to procure advanced weaponry, maintain military infrastructure, and invest in research and development for new technologies.
 
• The ranking considers the allocation of financial resources to defense-related activities as a critical element of a country's overall military strength.
 
• Countries with a larger and more consistent **defense budget** are typically better equipped to modernize their armed forces and maintain readiness.
 
• This factor is one of the most significant indicators of a nation's military might in terms of both quality and quantity of resources.
 
• Other elements of the ranking, such as manpower, equipment, and logistical capabilities, are often supported and enhanced by a robust **defense budget**.
 
• Leading nations like the **United States**, **China**, and **India** allocate substantial portions of their annual budgets to defense, which reflects their prioritization of national security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Economic Stability**__

 __
 
• **Economic stability** refers to a country's ability to maintain a steady rate of economic growth and avoid inflation or deflation.
 
• Although related to national strength, it is not directly assessed in the **Global Firepower Military Strength Ranking**.
 
• Economic stability often indirectly supports military strength by ensuring the availability of resources for defense spending.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Influence**__
 __
 
• **Cultural influence** pertains to a nation's ability to impact others through its culture, values, and traditions.
 
• It is a component of **soft power** rather than military or hard power, making it irrelevant to the **Global Firepower Military Strength Ranking**.
 
 
 
• **Healthcare Spending**__
 
 
• **Healthcare spending** involves a nation’s investment in the health and well-being of its citizens.
 
• While it contributes to a country's overall development and quality of life, it is not a parameter used in determining military strength.

questions.question: Which of the following **correctly **describes cooperative sector industries?

options.text: Owned and operated by central government agencies.
Owned by workers or suppliers sharing profits and losses
Maintained by foreign companies with Indian partnerships.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Owned by workers or suppliers sharing profits and losses**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cooperative sector industries** are those owned and managed by groups of individuals who share **common economic interests**. These groups often consist of **workers, suppliers, or consumers**.
 
• The primary objective is to ensure **mutual benefit**, where profits and losses are shared equally among all members.
 
• These industries follow the principle of **cooperation**, which promotes **economic equality** and prevents exploitation.
 
• Examples of cooperative sector industries include **milk cooperatives like Amul**, **handloom cooperatives**, and **agricultural cooperative societies**.
 
• Cooperatives play a crucial role in empowering rural areas by providing **employment**, **income stability**, and promoting **sustainable economic growth**.
 
• They also adhere to the democratic principle of **one member, one vote**, ensuring equitable decision-making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Owned and operated by central government agencies**__

 __
 
• Industries owned and operated by the **central government** fall under the category of **public sector industries**, not cooperative sector industries.
 
• These industries are managed by the government for purposes like **national development**, **security**, and providing essential services.
 
• Examples include **Indian Railways**, **BHEL**, and **ONGC**.
 
 
 
• **Operated solely for export purposes**__
 __
 
• Industries that primarily focus on **exports** are often classified as **export-oriented industries**.
 
• They aim to produce goods and services for **international markets** rather than domestic consumption.
 
• Examples include industries involved in **textiles**, **pharmaceuticals**, and **IT services** catering to global demand.
 
 
 
• **Maintained by foreign companies with Indian partnerships**__
 
 
• Industries maintained by foreign companies in collaboration with Indian entities are referred to as **joint ventures**.
 
• They aim to combine **resources**, **technology**, and **expertise** from both parties for mutual benefit.
 
• Examples include **Maruti Suzuki**, a joint venture between India's Maruti and Japan's Suzuki.

questions.question: Education is now placed under which list after the 42nd Amendment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concurrent List**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act of 1976** is one of the most comprehensive amendments to the Indian Constitution. It brought about significant changes in various provisions.
 
• One of the key changes was the transfer of **Education** from the **State List** to the **Concurrent List**.
 
• By placing education in the **Concurrent List**, both the **Union Government** and the **State Governments** can legislate on matters related to education.
 
• This amendment was aimed at achieving a **uniform educational policy** across the country, ensuring better coordination and implementation of educational reforms.
 
• The **Concurrent List** is one of the three legislative lists under the **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution of India. It contains subjects on which both the Union and State Governments can make laws.
 
• Other important subjects in the Concurrent List include **criminal law, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy, and forests**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Union List**__

 __
 
• The **Union List** contains subjects on which only the **Parliament** has exclusive powers to make laws.
 
• Examples of subjects in the Union List include **defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, banking, and communications**.
 
• It is mentioned in the **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution and includes **100 subjects**.
 
 
 
• **State List**__
 
 
• The **State List** contains subjects on which only the **State Legislatures** have the authority to legislate.
 
• Examples of subjects in the State List include **police, public health, agriculture, and local government**.
 
• This list also falls under the **Seventh Schedule** and contains **61 subjects**.

questions.question: What is the main objective of the National Framework for Climate Services (NFCS) launched in 2024?

options.text: To deliver sector-specific climate information services
To mandate carbon offsetting in the private sector

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**To deliver sector-specific climate information services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Framework for Climate Services (NFCS)** was launched in **2024** to provide climate information tailored to specific sectors.
 
• This framework aims to enhance **decision-making** and improve resilience in areas such as **agriculture, water resources, health, energy, and disaster management.**
 
• Its primary objective is to ensure the delivery of **timely, accurate, and actionable climate data** to stakeholders across various sectors.
 
• The NFCS aligns with **international frameworks**, such as the **Global Framework for Climate Services (GFCS)**, to promote better climate governance and collaboration.
 
• Sector-specific services include forecasting for **crop yields**, managing **water resources**, and planning for **energy distribution** based on climate patterns.
 
• By addressing the impacts of **climate change**, the NFCS supports sustainable development and helps mitigate risks associated with **climate variability and extreme weather events.**
 
• It also emphasizes **capacity building** and promotes collaboration between **scientists, policymakers, and stakeholders**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **To set emission trading targets**__

 __
 
• **Emission trading**, also known as **cap-and-trade**, is a market-based approach to control pollution by providing economic incentives for reducing emissions.
 
• This option relates to environmental economics rather than direct climate service delivery.
 
• India has previously introduced a **carbon market mechanism**, but it is not directly linked to the NFCS.
 
 
 
• **To regulate groundwater quality**__
 __
 
• Regulating **groundwater quality** involves policies to maintain water standards, often under **environmental protection acts**.
 
• While groundwater is affected by climate change, this is not the main objective of the NFCS.
 
• Groundwater regulation is generally managed by organizations like the **Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA)** in India.
 
 
 
• **To mandate carbon offsetting in the private sector**__
 
 
• **Carbon offsetting** involves compensating for emissions by investing in projects that reduce greenhouse gases.
 
• This option primarily pertains to corporate social responsibility and environmental policy, not climate service frameworks.
 
• India has introduced **carbon offset programs**, but the NFCS focuses more on providing climate data and services rather than mandates for offsetting.

questions.question: Argon is produced in Earth's crust via?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decay of K-40**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Argon** is a noble gas and is chemically inert, making it an important element in various industrial applications.
 
• On Earth, **Argon** is primarily produced through the **radioactive decay of Potassium-40 (K-40).**
 
• **K-40**, a naturally occurring isotope of potassium, undergoes **beta decay** to form **Argon-40 (Ar-40)**.
 
• This process occurs deep within the **Earth's crust** and contributes significantly to the presence of argon in the atmosphere.
 
• The Earth's atmosphere contains approximately **0.93% argon**, making it the third most abundant gas after nitrogen and oxygen.
 
• The decay of K-40 is a **long-term geological process** and is essential for understanding the Earth's isotopic composition and age.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Volcanoes**__

 __
 
• Volcanoes release various gases, including water vapor, carbon dioxide, sulfur dioxide, and sometimes traces of argon. However, argon from volcanic eruptions is minimal compared to its production through the decay of K-40.
 
• Volcanic activity contributes more significantly to the release of greenhouse gases like **CO₂** rather than inert gases like argon.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis**__
 __
 
• **Photosynthesis** is a biological process performed by plants, algae, and cyanobacteria to convert sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water into glucose and oxygen.
 
• It does not involve the production of argon or any other noble gases.
 
 
 
• **Cosmic rays**__
 
 
• Cosmic rays are high-energy particles from outer space. They can interact with the Earth's atmosphere to produce isotopes like **Carbon-14**, but they do not contribute significantly to the formation of argon in the Earth's crust.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about Fundamental Rights and DPSPs?

options.text: Both are justiciable and enforceable by courts
DPSPs override Fundamental Rights when in conflict
Fundamental Rights are justiciable, but DPSPs are not
DPSPs are guaranteed by the Constitution;Fundamental Rights are optional

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Fundamental Rights are justiciable, but DPSPs are not**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights** are explicitly mentioned in Part III of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• They are enforceable by the courts, meaning individuals can approach the courts if their rights are violated. This makes them **justiciable**.
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs)**, enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution, are not enforceable by the courts, making them **non-justiciable**.
 
• DPSPs act as guidelines for the government to achieve socio-economic goals and establish a welfare state.
 
• While **Fundamental Rights** focus on individual rights and liberties, DPSPs emphasize **collective welfare** and societal development.
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** has clarified that Fundamental Rights and DPSPs must be harmonized and not seen as conflicting entities.
 
• Examples of Fundamental Rights include the **Right to Equality** (Article 14-18) and the **Right to Freedom** (Article 19-22).
 
• Examples of DPSPs include the directive to promote **equal justice** and free legal aid (Article 39A) and to ensure **living wages** for workers (Article 43).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Both are justiciable and enforceable by courts**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because **only Fundamental Rights** are enforceable by courts, while DPSPs are not.
 
• DPSPs serve as principles for governance and cannot be legally upheld in courts.
 
 
 
• **DPSPs override Fundamental Rights when in conflict**__
 __
 
• The **Supreme Court** has ruled that Fundamental Rights hold a higher position in cases of conflict.
 
• However, efforts have been made to harmonize both, recognizing their complementary nature.
 
 
 
• **DPSPs are guaranteed by the Constitution; Fundamental Rights are optional**__
 
 
• This is incorrect as both Fundamental Rights and DPSPs are integral parts of the Constitution.
 
• Fundamental Rights are guaranteed and enforceable, while DPSPs are guidelines that cannot be enforced legally.
